pros: Detects negative weight cycles in the graph
Simpler implementation than Dijkstra for dense graphs
Works on both directed and undirected graphs
Can be distributed easily (local information only)
Dynamic programming foundation is theoretically elegant
Can be optimized with early termination
Provides foundation for distance-vector routing protocols
Allows negative costs in optimization problems
cons: Slower than Dijkstra: O(V·E) vs O((V+E) log V)
Must process all edges in each iteration (V-1 times)
Inefficient for sparse graphs with non-negative weights
High constant factor in time complexity
Memory access patterns can be cache-unfriendly
Not suitable for very large graphs (V·E may be huge)
Cannot compute all-pairs shortest paths efficiently
Struggles with graphs where V is large and dense
Requires V-1 iterations even for simple graphs without optimization
